prompt: Last year $30\%$ of a town's households recycled. After a campaign, a random sample of $200$ households finds $72$ recycling. For the test of $H_0: p = 0.30$ versus $H_a: p > 0.30$, what is the value of the test statistic $z$? Round to two decimal places.
hint: First find $\hat{p}$. Then $z = \frac{\hat{p} - p_0}{\sqrt{p_0(1-p_0)/n}}$, using the NULL value $p_0 = 0.30$ in the denominator.

hints.text: First find $\hat{p}$. Then $z = \frac{\hat{p} - p_0}{\sqrt{p_0(1-p_0)/n}}$, using the NULL value $p_0 = 0.30$ in the denominator.

explanation: $z = (0.36 - 0.30)/0.0324 \approx 1.85$. (For this one-sided test the $p$-value is about $0.032$, so at $\alpha = 0.05$ there is convincing evidence recycling increased.)

alternativeExplanations.title: Why p₀, not p̂, in the denominator
steps: A significance test asks: IF $p = 0.30$, how surprising is $\hat{p} = 0.36$?
So the spread must be computed under that assumption, with $0.30$: $SD \approx 0.0324$.
(A confidence interval, which makes no assumption about $p$, would use $\hat{p}$ instead.) $z \approx 1.85$.
